newsitem.title: ITALY: Slovenia, Belgium set to join Albania force.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia, Belgium set to join Albania force.

text.p: Slovenia will soon send a token contribution to the multinational force protecting the distribution of humanitarian aid in Albania, the Italian defence ministry said on Monday.
Riccardo Sessa, a senior defence ministry official, told a news briefing that a small contingent of around 30 men would be operating in Tirana from May 15.
Belgium was also considering sending troops to join the 6,000-strong force that began deploying in the impoverished Balkan state last month, he said.

The eight-nation Italian-led force has a mandate to secure ports and roads and protect the distribution of aid to Albania which was swept by a wave of violence after the collapse of fraudulent savings schemes earlier this year.
Sessa said the force had nearly reached its full strength of 6,500 troops, with almost 3,000 men from Italy.
Troops would now begin deployment from Tirana and Durres in central Albania and the southern port of Vlore towards the east and north of the country.
"The expansion into the interior has the objective of creating a network of security," he said, but adding that the troops would not act as a police force.

Spanish troops, now based in the northern town of Lezhe, were preparing to start deploying towards the northern town of Shkoder. A boat packed with more than 1,000 refugees set sail from near there on Saturday and arrived in Italy on Sunday.

Defence sources said on Saturday they thought thousands more Albanians were camped out near beaches in the north awaiting more ships to ferry them across the Adriatic to Italy, a journey already made by more than 14,000 people fleeing the unrest.
Sessa said that although the multinational force would deploy to the north it would not have the power to stop further boats leaving the Albanian coast.
"To think the force can be used against illegal immigration is a grave error," he said.

Under the three-month U.N. mandate given to the force, which comprises troops from Italy, France, Spain, Romania, Greece, Turkey, Austria and Denmark, soldiers are not in Albania to restore law and order to unruly areas or to act as police.
